body.text: I have had to shut {param:building} at {param:town}. There is no coin to run it and I will not pretend otherwise.
It stands where it stood. Nothing is pulled down and nothing is sold, and the day we can meet the charge it opens again — but until then it does nothing for us at all.
The people are {perception:spirits}, and they can see the doors shut as well as I can.
I had not thought to write you such a letter about a thing we built ourselves.
I would rather you heard it from me than found it in a ledger a year from now.

options.text: sorry you have had to do it
less surprised than I should like to be

steps.prompt: What is to come first at {param:town}

options.label: put the town back in profit
options.text: Put the town back in profit. A place that cannot meet its own charges is not a colony, it is an expense.

options.label: let it stand idle and see to your people
options.text: Let it stand idle. Doors can be opened again; the people cannot, and I would rather you had them fed than had the thing running.

options.label: the town is too small to carry it
options.text: The town is too small to carry what it has built. See that it grows, and the charge will stop looking so large.

tone.annoyed: See that it does not become a habit,
